treaty_name: Agreement between the United Kingdom and the Republic of Turkey for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income and capital gains (1986)
eif_quote: The double taxation agreement entered into force on 26 October 1988. It is effective in Turkey from 1 January 1989 and in the UK from: 1 April 1989 for Corporation Tax 6 April 1989 for Income Tax and Capital Gains Tax
source_title: 1988 UK-Turkey Double Taxation Agreement — in force (gov.uk HTML; signed 19 February 1986)

rates.quote: the tax so charged shall not exceed: (a) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company which controls directly or indirectly at least 25 per cent of the voting power in the company paying the dividends:
(b) 20 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.

However. such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the law of that State: but where the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

However, such royalties may be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the law of that State: but where the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

notes: Interest exempt at source when derived and beneficially owned by the other State's Government, local authority or agency, and UK-source interest beneficially owned by the Central Bank of Turkey (Art. 11(3)) — not modelled. Royalty definition includes industrial, commercial or scientific equipment rentals. Art. 10(4) allows a branch profits tax of up to 15%. valid_from = later of the two States' effective dates (Art. 28): Turkey 1 Jan 1989; UK 6 Apr 1989 (income tax) / 1 Apr 1989 (corporation tax). No protocol published on gov.uk. Not covered by the MLI (Türkiye not an MLI Party per treaties_merged.json) and the treaty contains no principal-purpose/main-purpose clause, so no PPT.
